raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "cantilever clamp and its coordinate convention",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 gives the domain (-1,1) × (-0.5,0.5), but calls x=0 its left boundary. The stated 3-D extension instead clamps x=-1.",
      "readings": [
        "Keep the stated domain and clamp its entire left edge at x=-1; treat x=0 as a typo.",
        "Keep the stated domain and constrain the internal line x=0, retaining the portion -1<x<0.",
        "Use the domain (0,1) × (-0.5,0.5), with the clamp at x=0 and load at x=1; treat the domain's lower x-bound as a typo."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "downward load at the right-edge midpoint",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 calls this a point load at the center, but specifies the finite segment x=1, -0.05<y<0.05. Eq. (3.16) treats t as a boundary traction.",
      "readings": [
        "Apply a concentrated force at (1,0).",
        "Apply a uniform downward traction over x=1, -0.05<y<0.05."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_magnitude",
      "entity": "normalization of the right-edge load",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1's combination of 'point load' and t=(0,-1) leaves resultant-force versus traction-density normalization unresolved. This only scales pure compliance, but can change layout when the paper's fixed Ginzburg–Landau and volume-penalty weights are retained.",
      "readings": [
        "On the stated patch, use t_y=-1, giving resultant F_y=-0.1 per unit thickness.",
        "Normalize the same patch to resultant F_y=-1, giving uniform t_y=-10."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "material retained around the clamp and load",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 specifies no passive-region mask or retained-solid pad dimensions. The uniform initialization does not explicitly specify whether any elements are subsequently frozen.",
      "readings": [
        "Allow all elements to vary; prescribe no passive regions.",
        "Keep one element layer adjacent to the loaded segment solid.",
        "Keep one element layer adjacent to both the clamp and loaded segment solid."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial volume-penalty coefficient",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.2 specifies only an O(1) initial lambda_penal. The known multiplier zeta=0.98 and 500 iterations do not determine the coefficient sequence without its initial value.",
      "readings": [
        "lambda_penal^(0)=0.5.",
        "lambda_penal^(0)=1.",
        "lambda_penal^(0)=2."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "timing of volume-penalty updates",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Section 4 says the penalty is updated after each outer loop, whereas Algorithm 1, line 16, updates it before that iteration's state and topology steps.",
      "readings": [
        "Use lambda_penal^(0)/0.98 for the first topology update.",
        "Use lambda_penal^(0) for the first topology update, then divide by 0.98 after the iteration."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "reference spectral bandwidths for case (a)",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Table 2 and Sec. 4.1.2 give displacement bandwidth 35 and topology bandwidth 30. Sec. 4.1.4's spectral study reverses these when identifying the reference case. These bandwidths affect the reference design representation; they are not a stated equivalent grid-filter radius.",
      "readings": [
        "Use topology bandwidth 30 and displacement bandwidth 35.",
        "Use topology bandwidth 35 and displacement bandwidth 30."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "finite-element cells and design-field discretization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.3 supplies a 120×60 FEM mesh, but does not specify cell topology, displacement interpolation, or phase-field interpolation. The APF 200×100 collocation grid identified in Sec. 4.1.4 does not supply these choices.",
      "readings": [
        "Use 120×60 bilinear quadrilaterals with nodal bilinear displacement and phase fields.",
        "Split each of 120×60 rectangular subdivisions into two linear triangles, with nodal linear displacement and phase fields.",
        "Use 120×60 bilinear displacement elements with elementwise design variables and a finite-difference discretization of the Ginzburg–Landau term."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "loaded-boundary quadrature allocation",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.2 describes 500 boundary points on the loaded and clamped segments together. Sec. 4.1.4 identifies the reference sampling as n_Gamma=500 on the nonhomogeneous Neumann boundary alone.",
      "readings": [
        "Use 500 points on the loaded segment; enforce the clamp analytically without clamp samples.",
        "Use 500 points total, split equally between loaded and clamped segments.",
        "Use 500 points total, allocated approximately by segment length: 45 loaded and 455 clamped."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "FEM phase-field pseudo-time step",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 2.1 and 4.1.3 describe pseudo-time evolution and give the outer and inner iteration counts, but provide no pseudo-time step or equivalent mobility-step product.",
      "readings": [
        "Use a constant effective pseudo-time step of 0.0001.",
        "Use a constant effective pseudo-time step of 0.001.",
        "Use a constant effective pseudo-time step of 0.01."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "FEM semi-implicit phase-field update",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.3 delegates the semi-implicit scheme to reference [21]; its update equations and stabilization choices are absent from the supplied text.",
      "readings": [
        "Treat the gradient-energy diffusion implicitly and the double-well derivative explicitly.",
        "Use convex splitting of the double-well potential with implicit diffusion.",
        "Use a stabilized linear semi-implicit update with implicit diffusion."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    }
  ]
}
